clue.text: Hot food aunt cooked without delay

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An aunt rustles up a hot meal in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' shuffles H (hot) with the letters of FOOD and AUNT; the phrase means immediately, as in dismissing an idea out of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something this way is doing it at once, on the spot, with no pause for thought.

clue.text: Two huge islands initially obscured in eclipse

indicators.note: obscured means hidden or muddled, so these letters are jumbled
initially picks the first letter of the word that comes before it

explanation.surface: During an eclipse two enormous islands are hidden from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscured' rearranges TWO and HUGE with I, the first letter of 'islands' picked by 'initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to surpass it, to count for more than it, as one argument may outrank another.

clue.text: Getting excited? Not entirely — just a shade

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, so the letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are thrilled and gets a lukewarm reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' signals letters taken from inside 'GetTING Excited'.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint trace of colour is a tinge, just as a slight shade of a colour is.

clue.text: Those who decide elections, in the main?

definitions.text: Those who decide elections, in the main?

parts.words: Those who decide elections, in the main?
parts.note: undecided electors swing results; read literally as voters drifting on the sea

explanation.surface: A question about who mostly settles the outcome of polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' suggests mostly, but the main is the sea, where floaters would bob.
explanation.definitionFit: Electors with no fixed party loyalty, who can swing a result, are known by this name.

clue.text: Green, endlessly outspoken, getting into trouble

indicators.note: getting into means the shortened word goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word for outspoken is cut off

parts.note: vocal means outspoken, expressing views freely

explanation.surface: An environmentalist, ceaselessly outspoken, lands in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: VOCAL loses its last letter for 'endlessly'; 'getting into' puts VOCA inside ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade of yellowish green is named after the fruit's skin and flesh.

clue.text: Society girl entertaining journalist, going over old times: case for the papers

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means sitting above, so this part is placed before what follows
entertaining means hosting, so the society girl holds the journalist inside

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A debutante hosts a reporter, reminiscing about the past, while looking for a document holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts ED inside DEB; in a down clue 'going over' sets that above O (old) and X (times).
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox for keeping legal documents such as property title papers.

clue.text: Regius Professor carrying a small file

indicators.note: one thing carrying another holds it within, so the abbreviation wraps the other letters

parts.note: RP is the abbreviation for a Regius Professor, a royal-chaired post at a British university
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A senior academic holds a small document folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts A and S (small) inside RP. The surface's 'file' is a folder of papers; the definition is the coarse metal tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse tool for shaping wood or metal is a type of file with raised teeth.

clue.text: Plant that's well, sort of, mostly infiltrated by military intelligence

indicators.note: infiltrated by means the other piece is slipped inside the shortened word
mostly means the final letter of the word for the well is dropped

parts.note: an artesian well is a sort of well where water rises under pressure

explanation.surface: A plant that is somewhat healthy has been penetrated by spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' reads as healthy, but it is a water well. ARTESIAN loses its N for 'mostly', and 'infiltrated by' puts MI inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood and mugwort belong to this genus of aromatic herbs and shrubs.

clue.text: Book penned by favourite academic purist

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the book is placed inside the word for favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
Dan is short for Daniel, a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A scholarly stickler writes a volume taken up by a well-liked author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like written, but here it means shut in, as in a pen; DAN (Daniel) goes inside PET.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who insists on fine points of learning or rules is a stickler of this kind.

clue.text: Steps taken in fog naturally in the wrong direction

indicators.note: in the wrong direction says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone picks their way carefully through mist, as one would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' signals letters held inside 'fog naturally', giving OGNAT, and 'in the wrong direction' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance is a set of steps, and this Argentine ballroom dance is a well-known example.

clue.text: Spoke about backward clergyman with unjustified reputation

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for spoke goes around the other piece

parts.note: orated means spoke formally, as in giving a speech

indicators.note: backward tells us the abbreviation for the clergyman is read from right to left

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: Someone talked about a reactionary vicar who was not as good as people claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns REV into VER, and 'about' puts ORATED around it, splitting O from RATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thought better than it truly is enjoys a reputation it does not deserve.

clue.text: Greek princess's cunning personality almost taken the wrong way

indicators.note: taken the wrong way says the combined letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: art can mean cunning or craft, as in artful

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word for a personality is lost

parts.note: a celeb, short for celebrity, is a famous personality

explanation.surface: A Greek royal has a sly character that is easily misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: CELEB loses its last letter for 'almost' to give CELE; ART + CELE is then turned round by 'taken the wrong way'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the daughter of Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, who avenged his murder.

clue.text: Speaker at union meeting

parts.note: the union is a marriage, not a trade union, and the meeting is the wedding reception where a groom's friend gives a speech

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a gathering of trade unionists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union meeting' suggests a trade union assembly; read it as a wedding, where this friend of the groom traditionally makes a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The groom's chief attendant traditionally gives a speech at the wedding reception.

clue.text: Donated too generously, being quite extreme in one's habits?

definitions.meaning: handed over more than was needed
inclined to overindulge, prone to doing things to excess

explanation.surface: A philanthropist overdoes the giving because they are immoderate by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the words literally: handed over too much. The second takes the phrase as an idiom for a habitual tendency to overdo things.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally handed over more than needed; idiomatically, habitually inclined to overindulge.

clue.text: Bloodthirsty activity

parts.note: bloodthirsty usually means violent, but here it is taken literally as craving blood to drink

explanation.surface: A savage spree of violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloodthirsty' means cruel in everyday use; read literally, it is the thirst for blood of the undead of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of drinking blood, as legendary undead creatures do, is literally thirsting for blood.

clue.text: Frank's hetero

definitions.meaning: honest and direct, as in giving a ... answer

explanation.surface: A man named Frank declares his sexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' at the start looks like a man's name, but it means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid speaking is plain and direct; informally the same word also describes a heterosexual person.

clue.text: Whitsun picnic, possibly

parts.note: a church festival whose date shifts each year, read literally as a meal eaten on the move

explanation.surface: A family spread laid out on a bank holiday outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitsun, the church feast of Pentecost, falls on a different date each year; a picnic is also a feast that can be carried about.
explanation.definitionFit: A church festival whose date changes from year to year, like Easter or Pentecost, is so called; a portable meal fits too.

clue.text: Examiner's car stuck on hill

indicators.note: in a down clue stuck on means placed on top, so the car comes above the hill

parts.note: Audi is a make of German car
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in south-west England

explanation.surface: An inspector's vehicle is stranded on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'stuck on' sets AUDI above TOR, a rocky hilltop of the kind found on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who officially inspects accounts is an examiner of financial records.

clue.text: Plague? Curse, mostly,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Plague? Curse, mostly, (7)' is cut short: 'Curse, mostly' gives at most CUS(S), and the rest of the wordplay is missing; no scan or search supplies it.

clue.text: View from space changed over time

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the rearranged letters sit before the final piece
changed means altered, so the letters of the word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The view from outer space has altered as the years go by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges SPACE to give ASPEC, which 'over' puts above T (time) in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlook or prospect, such as a south-facing one, is the direction a building faces.

clue.text: Is listed as 'stiff and pompous'

parts.note: the contraction 's stands for is, giving S
a ship that has listed has leaned over, or tilted

explanation.surface: Something is entered in a register with a description of being formal and stuffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listed' reads as entered in a list, but here it is a ship leaning to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or writing that is formal, laboured and unnatural is described with this word.

clue.text: Stuff mostly seen around 5 cavity indicates disease

indicators.note: around tells us the shortened word for stuff wraps the other piece
mostly means the last letter of the word for stuff is dropped

parts.note: to cram is to stuff something full
a hole is a cavity or hollow

explanation.surface: Something stuffed into a hollow is a sign of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: CRAM loses its last letter for 'mostly' to give CRA, and 'around' puts it on either side of HOLE: C-HOLE-RA.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute bacterial infection of the intestine, spread by dirty water, is this disease.

clue.text: Irish expert's about to turn up in plant

indicators.note: in a down clue to turn up means read from bottom to top, so the letters are reversed
about means around, so the word for expert surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: an ace is an expert, and the 's here is just a link

explanation.surface: An Irish specialist is about to appear in a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IR inside ACE to make ACIRE, and 'to turn up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather belongs to this genus of low evergreen shrubs.

clue.text: Undergoes a change of state

parts.note: reads like physics, a solid turning to liquid, but means moving to live in another country

explanation.surface: A substance melts or freezes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of state' sounds like a physical transition such as melting; here state means a nation, and the change is of residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone leaving their homeland to settle in another country moves from one state to another.

clue.text: Looking at conclusion of biography, one written in English

indicators.note: written in means the following letters are placed inside the abbreviation
conclusion of picks the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Reading the end of a life story that was penned in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion of biography' gives Y and 'one' gives I; 'written in' puts YI inside ENG.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching or regarding something closely is a synonym for looking at it.

clue.text: Issue that's about apprenticeship, typically

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for issue is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to issue or send out

explanation.surface: A dispute over trainee schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun (a matter or a magazine number) but is the verb, EMIT, which 'about' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice serves a fixed period of training, so an apprenticeship is an example of a period served.

clue.text: Electric train sets withstanding adverse conditions

indicators.note: electric suggests something charged and jumping about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Model railway sets that survive rough treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electric' seems to describe the train sets but is the anagram signal for TRAIN SETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to hold out against harsh conditions is resistant, as in weather-proof.
